messages:
Alex: Quick thread 1: thinking through fastpath admission for dedicated GPU pools. Two options on the table: (1) lightweight fastpath lane that lets short/low-latency requests bypass soft reservations, or (2) strictly honor soft reservations and rely on autoscaler to absorb spikes. Which gives best predictability for SLOs and cost?
Maria: Fastpath improves tail but it's a fairness footgun if unmetered. If we keep it it needs strict tenant caps and clear billing signals.
Jamal: On billing: fastpath should consume a distinct warmup credit or premium meter. Ops can't troubleshoot cost without a signal.
Sasha: Also think about eviction accounting. If a reserved request is evicted to make room for fastpath, we need a transparent refund or logged event.
Kevin: Operator note: prefer keeping admission decisions declarative. Control plane should own credit accounting and weights; operator enforces node-level utilization and placement.
Anya: Agree on separation. Operator can emit a short-lived in-memory lease for in-flight allocations, but no long-term accounting. Heartbeats + reconcile should be fine.
Alex: Draft policy DSL idea for discussion:

policy:
  tiers:
    - name: fastpath
      max_concurrency: 40
      warmup_credit_cost_per_request: 2
      fallback: reserved
    - name: reserved
      fairness: weighted
      min_headroom: 0.06
autoscaler:
  scale_target_util: 0.82
  emergency_disable_fastpath_if_util_over: 0.94

Maria: Couple of practical points: 1) per-tenant cooldown windows so noisy tenants can't instant-refill via retries, 2) fairness weights must be adjustable at tenant granularity.
Jamal: Simulator should test three shapes: spiky tiny requests, sustained throughput, and long-decoding sessions. We need cost/delta and eviction counts.
Sasha: Fragmentation: small fastpath allocations increase fragmentation on MIG/slot nodes. Admission should add a fragmentation penalty or prefer exact-slot nodes.
Kevin: We'll add prefer_node_hint: exact_slot_size and a fragmentation metric. Operator will expose an emergency gate to disable fastpath per-shard if saturation persists.
Anya: Canary plan: enable on one shard with observability hooks. Key metrics: tenant_fastpath_hits_total, tenant_fastpath_fallbacks_total, tenant_warmup_credit_balance, tenant_evictions_total, per_shard_gpu_utilization, p95_latency_by_tier. Auto-disable thresholds: evictions > 50 in 10m for any tenant, or p95 latency regression > 20%.
Alex: Ops-bot can we create a deploy-gate key for canary toggles?
ops-bot: Deploy gate registered: /deploy-gate set fastpath_canary shard=us-west-2b. Use `/deploy-gate status fastpath_canary`. :white_check_mark:
Maria: Implementation notes: - charge fastpath requests immediately (atomic decrement) - on eviction refund credits and increment tenant_evictions_total - enforce cooldown by rejecting fastpath for tenants who retried > N times in M sec.
Jamal: Need a clear pricing note in the docs: fastpath per-request multiplier and warmup credit top-up rules. Also UX for tenants to see their balance.
Sasha: Edgecases: cross-shard allocation (request routed to shard without matching slots) should fallback to reserved, not fastpath. Also consider a soft degradation path that gradually reduces fastpath concurrency rather than flipping off.
Kevin: Operator will maintain in-memory leases and expose /metrics for fragmentation and in-flight counts. Control plane reconciler will own weights and credit balances.
Anya: Action items:
- Jamal/Maria: define warmup-credit economics and cooldown parameters
- Sasha/Kevin: operator changes for emergency disable, fragmentation metric, and lease heartbeats
- Alex/Anya: simulator scenarios and canary thresholds + dashboard widgets

Alex: I'll open a follow-up RFC with the DSL, simulation results, and rollout checklist later today. Thanks everyone. :tada:
